page: Amazon Web Services c9g.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton architecture. The instance provides 96 dedicated physical cores based on the Neoverse-V3 core design running at 3.3 GHz, with a 1:1 mapping of virtual CPUs to physical cores without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation stands at 192.0 GB, delivering a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration features an L3 cache of 96 MB, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 64 KB of L1 data cache per core. Networking bandwidth offers a 50 Gbps baseline. No GPUs are attached, and local instance storage is absent, requiring external block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark measurements show high parallel compute and memory throughput. In multi-core evaluation, the instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core score of 192014.4, placing in the top tier. Cached read-only memory bandwidth reached 13912.96 GB/sec, while uncached 256 MB block reads and writes reached 363.83 GB/sec and 168.26 GB/sec respectively. PassMark memory testing scored 4603.51, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered 1131.71 GB/sec. Data operations show strong metrics, including 269.45 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, a PassMark database score of 57730.61, and static web serving throughput of 198.56 GB/sec. For small-model LLM prompt processing (135M), it reached 4506.32 tokens/sec, though single-core stress-ng performance scored in the average band at 2007.4.

The 96-core dedicated non-hyperthreaded topology offers high hardware density and computational isolation, resulting in favorable operational efficiency for parallelized ARM-native binaries. Because it lacks onboard NVMe storage, workloads that rely heavily on high-speed scratch space must factor in network storage latency. The instance fits high-throughput compute tasks, batch data processing, distributed compression, web-scale caching layers, and containerized microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 96 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 physical cores at 3.3 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 192.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside a 96 MB L3 cache and a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage. In benchmark assessments, c9g.24xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded compute and data handling, recording 192014.4 in stress-ng multi-core, 269.45 million Redis SET operations per second, and 198.56 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Single-core performance remains average. Given its high core density and memory throughput, the instance is well suited for batch compute jobs, compression pipelines, large-scale Redis in-memory caches, and high-concurrency web services.
